name: Modern SEO M3 L1: What the Core 30 Framework Is
body:
> Module 3, 4:27. Source: Lesson 1 What the Core 30 Framework Is.mp4

## In short
- Core 30 is the instructor's advanced system for competitive markets, used when the three-step method stalls (rank map stuck below 10% to 15% green after 8 to 10 weeks).
- Core 30 means building a website page for every category and every service listed on the Google Business Profile (GBP), then structuring and internally linking those pages exactly like the GBP is organized.
- The goal is "massive topical relevance": showing Google dedicated content for everything the business does instead of making it guess.
- Core 30 will not fix fundamental problems (technical, authority). It is for businesses with solid fundamentals that have plateaued.
- Once the rank map reaches 20% to 40% green, topical relevance is usually enough and the focus shifts to geographic relevance (neighborhoods and landmarks).

## Key ideas
- **When to use it.** Use Core 30 when the three-step method is not enough: the rank map is stuck below 10% to 15% green coverage after 8 to 10 weeks. Basic GBP optimization and citations are not sufficient to break through in these markets (0:02, slide at 0:25).
- **What it is.** One page on the website for every GBP category and every GBP service. The site structure and internal links mirror the GBP hierarchy, so what Google sees on the GBP lines up with what it finds on the website (0:20 to 0:37).
- **Why it works.** Comprehensive coverage gives Google dedicated, relevant content for any service someone searches for. The instructor calls the goal "massive, topical relevance" (0:38).
- **Page structure (three levels)** (0:58 to 1:33):
  - Home page: primary GBP category plus city name (examples on slide: Plumber Houston, Air Conditioning Repair Denver).
  - Category pages: one per secondary GBP category (examples: Gas Line Installation, Drain Cleaning Service).
  - Service pages: one per service listed under that category on the GBP (examples under Drain Cleaning Service: Emergency Drain Cleaning, Main Sewer Line Cleaning, Kitchen Drain Cleaning).
- **Internal linking mirrors the GBP** (1:36 to 1:57, slide at 2:05):
  - Home page links to the category pages and maybe one or two critical services (example: "Water heater replacement" for a plumber).
  - Category pages link to their relevant service pages.
  - Service pages link back to their parent category and up to the home page.
- **URL structure does not matter.** The instructor says Google works on internal links, not URL paths (2:02).
- **Fundamentals come first.** If a site has 450 indexed URLs and still ranks 20+ for its primary keyword when standing in the business's lobby, Core 30 is not the fix. That points to basic technical issues, authority problems, or other fundamental issues (2:07 to 2:26).
- **Who it is for.** Businesses that implemented the three-step method correctly, saw some ranking improvements, then plateaued because competitors have more comprehensive content coverage (2:30 to 2:39). The instructor says this typically happens in markets over 500,000 population or any market with multiple strong competitors who already have comprehensive websites (2:47).
- **When to stop.** Keep watching the rank map during implementation. At about 20% to 40% green coverage, topical relevance is usually enough for the market. Then shift to geographic relevance: content about the specific neighborhoods and landmarks served (3:05 to 3:25).
- **Positioning.** Core 30 "bridges the gap between basic local SEO and advanced content strategy." More work than the three-step method, but necessary in competitive markets (3:48).

## Step-by-step process
1. Confirm the three-step method is done correctly and the rank map has plateaued (stuck below 10% to 15% green after 8 to 10 weeks) (0:02, 2:37).
2. Rule out fundamental problems first (technical issues, authority problems). If the business ranks 20+ for its primary keyword from its own lobby despite many indexed URLs, fix those first (2:12 to 2:26).
3. List every GBP category and service. Fill them into the instructor's PowerPoint template to see which pages are missing and how to structure them (3:30).
4. Build the pages: home page (primary category + city), one category page per secondary category, one service page per GBP service under its category (1:00 to 1:33).
5. Link the pages to mirror the GBP hierarchy (home to categories and one or two critical services, categories to services, services back to category and home) (1:36 to 1:57).
6. Keep watching the rank map. At 20% to 40% green, shift focus to geographic relevance (neighborhood and landmark content) (3:05 to 3:25).
7. Next lesson: run a Core 30 gap analysis to find what is missing (4:05).

## Checklist
- Rank map checked: stuck below 10% to 15% green after 8 to 10 weeks of the three-step method.
- Fundamentals ruled out (no basic technical or authority problems).
- Home page targets primary GBP category + city name.
- One category page exists for each secondary GBP category.
- One service page exists for every GBP service, placed under its category.
- Home page links to all category pages (plus one or two critical services).
- Each category page links to its service pages.
- Each service page links back to its parent category and the home page.
- Rank map re-checked during the build; switch to geographic relevance at 20% to 40% green.

## Tools and resources mentioned
| Tool or resource | What it is used for | Timestamp |
|---|---|---|
| Rank map | Measures green (top 3) coverage; tells you when to start Core 30 and when to move on | 0:02, 3:05 |
| Google Business Profile (GBP) | Source of the categories and services that define the page list and hierarchy | 0:20 |
| Core 30 PowerPoint template (downloadable with the lesson) | Fill in current GBP categories and services to see missing pages and structure | 3:30 |

## Numbers and benchmarks
These are the instructor's claims, not verified facts.
- Below 10% to 15% green rank map coverage after 8 to 10 weeks: time to use Core 30 (0:02).
- 450 indexed URLs and ranking 20+ for the primary keyword from the business lobby: Core 30 is not the solution (2:12).
- Core 30 situations typically happen in markets over 500,000 population (2:47).
- 20%, 30%, 40% green coverage on the rank map: usually enough topical relevance; shift to geographic relevance (3:14).

## Terms
**Core 30:** Building a website page for every GBP category and service, structured and internally linked to match the GBP hierarchy.
**Three-step method:** The basic method from Modules 1 and 2 (GBP audit and fix, GBP landing page audit and fix, quality citations) that comes before Core 30.
**Topical relevance:** How completely the website covers the services the business offers. Core 30's main output.
**Geographic relevance:** Content about the specific neighborhoods and landmarks a business serves. The next focus after Core 30.
**Green coverage:** The share of the rank map grid where the business ranks in the top 3.
**Category page:** A page targeting one secondary GBP category.
**Service page:** A page targeting one service listed under a GBP category.

## Worth quoting
- "Core 30 means building a page on your website for every single category and every single service listed on your Google Business Profile." (0:20)
- "URL structure is not important with this. Google works on internal links." (2:02)
- "Core 30 is for businesses that have solid fundamentals but need more topical relevance to compete in their market." (2:30)

## How to use this at TAG
- **Check the trigger first.** Before proposing Core 30 for Pipeliners, Alphalete, or Summit AZ, Kim can pull each client's current rank map and compare it to the lesson's trigger (stuck below 10% to 15% green after 8 to 10 weeks of the three-step work).
- **Fundamentals gate for Alphalete.** Kim's project memory (`project_alphalete_gsc_indexing.md`) records that in June 2026 only 3 of 244 Alphalete pages were indexed, with orphaned /services/ city pages and sitemap problems. By this lesson's rule, indexing and technical issues come before Core 30. Recommendation: confirm current indexing status in Google Search Console before planning Core 30 pages.
- **Map each GBP to the three levels.** For each client, list the primary GBP category (home page target with city), each secondary category (category page), and each GBP service (service page). The PowerPoint template from this lesson is built for this.
- **Summit AZ fits the lesson's own example.** The lesson's examples are plumbing (Plumber + city, Drain Cleaning Service, Gas Line Installation, water heater replacement as a critical service), so the structure can be applied almost directly to summitplumbingpros.com's GBP categories and services.
- **Internal linking is the lever, not URLs.** When reviewing client sites, focus recommendations on links (home to category, category to service, service back up) rather than changing URL paths. Client sites are read-only for Claude, so these go to Kim as a list of recommended link additions.
- **Know when to stop.** At 20% to 40% green, the lesson says shift to neighborhood and landmark content.

## Open questions
- The lesson does not explain why it is called "Core 30" (the number is never defined). Lesson 3 suggests most businesses need 15 to 25 new pages, so "30" may be an approximate page count (unclear in video).
- The "lobby test" (rank 20+ from the business lobby) uses 450 indexed URLs as the example. It is not stated whether that number is a threshold or just an illustration.
- The 500,000 population figure is a rough guide from the instructor; no source is given.
- The PowerPoint template is "below the lesson" on the course page. It is not in the video files; Kim needs to download it from the course.
- Transcript fixes from slides: "Plummer Houston" is "Plumber Houston"; "GPP categories" is "GBP categories"; "implementation progress" is "implementation process" (3:05, slide title at 3:25).
- The slide at 2:25 was captured mid-build mid-build ("basic technical issues, authority problems"); the spoken version adds "or other fundamental issues."

## Timestamps
- 0:02 When to use Core 30 (three-step method stalls)
- 0:20 Definition: a page for every GBP category and service
- 0:38 Goal: massive topical relevance
- 0:58 Structure: home page, category pages, service pages
- 1:36 Internal linking that mirrors the GBP
- 2:02 URL structure does not matter
- 2:07 Lobby test: when Core 30 is not the answer
- 2:30 Who Core 30 is for (plateaued businesses)
- 2:47 Typical markets (over 500,000 population, strong competitors)
- 3:05 Watch the rank map; 20% to 40% green means shift to geographic relevance
- 3:30 PowerPoint template
- 3:48 Summary: bridges basic local SEO and advanced content strategy
- 4:05 Preview of the gap analysis lesson
